# Dummedhajātaka (Ja 122)
**ID:** Ja 122
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Dummedhajātaka* (Ja 122) is a short birth story located in the *Ekanipāta* of the Pali Jātaka collection [Fausböll 1877; Anandajoti 2010]. The verse begins with the line *Yasaṁ laddhāna dummedho, anatthaṁ carati attano* ("When a fool acquires fame, he acts to his own ruin") [Anandajoti 2010; Fausböll 1877]. According to the prose commentary (*atthuppatti*), the Buddha related this story while residing at the Bamboo Grove (Veḷuvana) in Rājagaha concerning Devadatta, whose jealousy was aroused by the sight of the Buddha's bodily perfections and the great honor accorded to him [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1877].
In the story of the past (*atītavatthu*), the Bodhisatta was reborn as a magnificent royal elephant, his future disciple Ānanda was his mahout, and Devadatta was a jealous king of Magadha [Olson 2015; Anandajoti 2010]. Resentful of the admiration shown toward the elephant, the king sought to have the animal plunge to its death from a mountain precipice by issuing increasingly perilous commands, challenging the mahout to have the elephant balance on three legs, two legs, and ultimately on a single leg at the edge of the abyss [Olson 2015; Anandajoti 2010]. Having demonstrated its extraordinary training and exposed the king's malicious folly, the elephant departed for another realm [Anandajoti 2010]. This story must be distinguished from the homonymous *Dummedhajātaka* (Ja 50), which tells of a prince who puts an end to animal sacrifices made to a tree-spirit [Appleton 2010; Sutherland 1991; DeCaroli 2004].
Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus identifies any cross-language parallels or significant Pali-internal text reuse for this text, though SuttaCentral records translations into four languages [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
